She has nobody in Bishkek.
She loves only you alone.
Then why did she lie to me?

Now she has to fly away urgently.
She will come to Moscow in five years.
You have your work and mother here.
She decided not to stand in your way.
In two hours she will fly away.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С возвращением тебя к нам, Витя!
examples.trans: Welcome back to us, Vitya!
But a special thank you to my son-in-law.

examples.text: Папа, он пока ещё не зять.
examples.trans: Dad, he is not your son-in-law yet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Misha, thank you for everything.
Heavy work is forbidden for you right now.

examples.text: Всю жизнь я за тебя боялась.
examples.trans: All my life I was afraid for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That title will be his in twenty-four hours.
This is our new head chef.
Really, and who is this man?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will kill', paired with 'убивать'.

examples.trans: Then take away my signature menu!

I'll kill you! (said in anger)

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: But a special thank you to my son-in-law.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Папа, он пока ещё не зять.
examples.trans: Dad, he is not your son-in-law yet.
Vitya, you must not get nervous at all.
I actually like this idea.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.

meanings.en: to be silent, to keep quiet

examples.trans: But I cannot keep silent.

examples.text: Ну что ты молчишь? Ты толстый, ты не спортсмен!

examples.trans: After all, you love her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Почему вы лезете на мою кухню?
examples.trans: Why are you meddling in my kitchen?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am allowed, I am not the groom.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оврать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lie, tell a lie', paired with 'врать'.

examples.trans: Then why did she lie to me?

examples.text: Потому что я соврал про деньги.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'срочиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'expired'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и просрочиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and expired on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют просрочиться.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will arrive', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Wait, have we arrived already?
